meta.howToUse: Publish each entry's `record` with com.atproto.repo.putRecord (repo=cultureblocs.com, collection, rkey). Everything outside `record` is sidecar metadata for the site and is not published.
meta.timezone: Times are Europe/London, GMT (+00:00) throughout: the clocks went back on 25 October 2026, before the festival.
meta.checked: Every programme item read from the festival's Ticket Tailor page on 25 October 2026 (tools/events/games_transformed_2026_source.txt). Venue addresses from venue listings and Pelican House's own box office.
meta.timesTbc: The festival gives no times, rooms or speakers for individual sessions. Sessions are date-only (startsAt 00:00, no endsAt) and show as 'Time tbc'; games run from Saturday 10:00 to Sunday 19:30. Update and republish when a timetable appears.
meta.prices: From the box office checkout on 25 October 2026, plus booking fees: weekend pass £45 standard / £55 final release; Saturday or Sunday day pass £25; under-16 day ticket £15; Friday evening social £5; motherlode party £12 (not in day or weekend passes). Solidarity tickets on request.
meta.omitted: Nothing in the programme is left out. Descriptions are our own short summaries; the organisers' copy stays on their page.
meta.unofficial: Independent listing by CultureBlocs; not affiliated with or endorsed by Games Transformed or any listed game, maker or venue.

record.name: Games Transformed Festival 2026
record.description: A festival of games and radical politics in Bethnal Green, East London, run by the volunteer-led Games Transformed. The 2026 theme, Here to Stay, Here to Play, echoes the 1970s East London anti-racist slogan Here to Stay, Here to Fight: racial and migrant justice as one struggle, and games as a way to resist. Over 80 games, plus panels, workshops, performance, a youth and families programme and the motherlode afterparty, across Proposition Studios, Pelican House and Three Colts Tavern. Friday 18:30–23:00, Saturday 10:00–18:30 (afterparty from 20:00), Sunday 10:00–19:30. Weekend and day passes; the Friday social and the afterparty are ticketed separately. Free or discounted solidarity tickets are available by email. Umbrella record: the events in this collection reference the same festival.

locations.name: Proposition, Pelican House or Three Colts Tavern, Bethnal Green

records.notes: Unofficial umbrella record; not published by Games Transformed. The box office header gives Fri 18:00 – Sun 19:30; the page's own When? section says Friday 18:30, which we use.

record.name: Games Against Borders symposium and evening social
record.description: The festival opens with the ReImagining Value Action Lab's Games Against Borders symposium, then a relaxed social evening of games and a chance to meet other players and organisers. Ticketed separately as the Friday evening social: £5 + £1 booking fee.

locations.name: Proposition, Pelican House or Three Colts Tavern, Bethnal Green

records.notes: The page's When? section gives Friday 18:30–23:00; the ticket is named 'Evening Social from 6pm'. Venue not stated.

record.name: MONSTREOUS Costume and Cosplay Competition
record.description: The Halloween costume theme is monsters — monstrosity as political, the label pinned on those who challenge the established order. Prizes, including free games and festival tickets, for the most MONSTREOUS outfits across Saturday's day and night programme.

locations.name: Proposition, Pelican House or Three Colts Tavern, Bethnal Green

records.notes: Runs across Saturday's day and night programme; no judging time given.

record.name: motherlode afterparty
record.description: The Games Transformed afterparty takes over all three venues from 8pm till late: DJs including Bledi, Dance Against Deportations and Nachtlicker, live coding, shibari performance, cross-venue quests, an immersive chill space, games and the costume competition. Not included in day or weekend passes: party ticket £12 + £1 booking fee.

locations.name: Proposition, Pelican House or Three Colts Tavern, Bethnal Green

records.notes: The page says 8pm (twice); the ticket is named 'from 7pm'. We use 20:00. Ends 'till late', so no endsAt.

record.name: What a State!?
record.description: The youth and families programme, for ages 8 and up (8–88, younger children welcome to join in): an immersive world of absurd challenges and bureaucracy, built around a Very Completely Official British Citizenship Test. Saturday and Sunday. Under-16 day tickets £15 + £1 booking fee; a crèche run with Nanny Solidarity Network is available — tell the festival in advance.

locations.name: Proposition, Pelican House or Three Colts Tavern, Bethnal Green

records.notes: The page says the youth and families programme runs all day on both days; we give it festival hours.
